- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast spikes upward, cap the next 3–5 periods’ forecast to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is high, apply downward bias of 1–2% per period to reflect bearish momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), reduce subsequent forecast by 0.5–1.5% per period to correct for overreaction.  
- If true price deviates from forecast by >3% in early periods (1–3), assume mean reversion and adjust forecast toward historical mean of last 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.7) and forecast is consistently above true, apply a 1–2% downward correction to the next 3 periods.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, avoid sharp upward trends; favor gradual, low-volatility trajectories.  
- If true price drops sharply after a forecast peak, assume sentiment shift and reduce forecast slope for next 5 periods.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), apply a 1–3% downward bias to all forecasts.
